newsitem.title: UK: Raine upbeat on current trading.
newsitem.headline: Raine upbeat on current trading.

text.p: British housebuilding and contracting company Raine Plc said on Thursday that operating results for its core activities have improved in the first four months of its financial year over the same period of last year.
Chairman Roy Barber told the company's annual general meeting, "I am confident that the reorganised group will continue to make satisfactory progress for the balance of 1996 and 1997."
Raine announced in October that it made pretax profit of 0.57 million stg for the year ended June 30, 1996 from a loss of 102 million stg in the previous year.

The company, having launched a reorganisation programme in 1995, said it has dealt most problems that had accumulated before 1995, but it will take some more time to correct its high borrowings priority and under-investment in householding land.
In its October report Raine said its net borrowings at 30 June 1996 were 36.4 million stg, down from 50.7 million stg the year before.

Raine said that Hassall Homes, its domestic private housing member, experienced an encouraging level of activity in the three months ended September 30, 1996, but said this did not continue in October and November.
"However, I expect Hassall Homes to achieve in excess of 600 sales from 70 selling outlets in the current half year," Barber said. "This reflects an increase of 10 percent in the sales per outlet."
Market conditions in the spring of 1997, possibly influenced by the run up to the elections, will be key for the unit's annual results, he said.

Hall & Tawse improved in both building contracting which continues to perform in line with Raine's expectations, and in social housing, which is maintaining its profitability despite the falling market opportunities which result in lower turnover.
Raine's Californian housebuilding unit, West Venture is expected to make an operating profit for the current half year but it was likely to remain below that in the same period of 1995.
At 1113 GMT Raine's shares stood at 13.75p, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
